follow-on: both suite fields name `command` with angle-bracket placeholders — `pytest -n 10 -p no:cacheprovider -q --rootdir=<base tree> <the 166 test files importing reckon.crew.recovery>` — rather than the literal command that ran; the dispatch contract requires the literal command with absolute paths and no placeholder, and the placeholders are why the base arm's working directory cannot be resolved to reduce its ids.

justifications.durability: the new behaviour is guarded by committed tests — the dry-run test lists the plan's report root before and after two previews and asserts it unchanged, the real-dispatch test asserts the directory and its brief/snapshot/sidecar, and the negative control reddens the first when the early write returns. The guard is scoped to the report root, so a preview that wrote anywhere else (e.g. a live pointer or the shared config home) would not be caught, and the scratch brief staging is not asserted to be removed.
justifications.evidence: the runnable core evidence reproduces — focused gate 21 passed at head, and I independently restored the early write (`write=False`→`write=True` at recovery.py:2310 in a scratch copy of head) and the dry-run test reddened with EXIT=1 (1 failed, 20 passed), and I verified the listing assertion fires under the same mutation once the earlier assertion is removed. justifications.fit: the change extends the single composer with a `write` flag rather than forking a second one, and `_standing_plan_review` removes a duplicated in-flight scan — the right factoring. Two costs: the preview stages the brief into a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` so `plan_dispatch` can digest it, a scratch round-trip the real path avoids; and the sidecar path is built from the private `plan_review._REVIEW_SIDECAR_NAME` across the module boundary, where a public accessor would keep the coupling honest.
